admission.justification: The Jump-only behavior and the answered-only reveal were weighed and rejected, and every later change to how a tree row or a kept family is selected has to decide what the stacked layout shows and what it leaves to the reader's next action.

alternatives.option: An explicit subject selection arms one landing to the subject's heading when its read settles, unless the reader has scrolled since the click. Focus and tree-local row reveal have separate owners; an eligible failed/refused selection lands focus once and retains its focus request for Retry.
alternatives.reason: OR-R033 and OR-R042 established that one activation must show the selected answer or failed/refused status without requiring a second Jump. The approved MIK-R89 v2 rule 9 now gives the reading column one landing after a selection's read, cancelled by reader scrolling; the v2 page replaces the former 60rem stacked-only implementation. This account states the installed A4-F5 behavior and makes no new page-jump acceptance claim.

alternatives.option: Keep the explicit Jump control as the only way to the reading area, as before the ruling.
alternatives.reason: An in-tree selection that appears to do nothing until the reader finds a second control is the measured defect the ruling exists to fix.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The stacked layout stops placing the reading area below a tall tree, so a selection already shows its answer without a reveal.

alternatives.option: Reveal only when the read is answered; a failed or refused selection keeps the view where it was.
alternatives.reason: OR-R042 closed this alternative: the failed or refused status is what the reading area has to show for that selection, and the owner ruled there is no answered-only exception.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The status of a failed or refused read is shown somewhere the reader already sees, so the reading area need not be revealed for it.

consequences: A selection arms one reading target. Once the selected subject's read is no longer loading, the page spends that target and lands once unless the reader has disarmed it by scrolling; the tree is never scrolled by that landing owner.
Above 40rem the reading column scrolls itself; at 40rem and narrower the surrounding page scrolls and the target is brought into view. This is a source account, not a browser geometry grade.

Eligible focus lands on the target-state notice or current tree row with preventScroll. Failed/refused selection focus lands once and keeps the request for Retry; a reader who moved focus keeps that focus. This focus guard is distinct from cancellation of the reading landing by reader scrolling.
The explicit Jump control and revealUnavailableRead are removed; neither is retained as an alternative route or a current source anchor.
